deep.reconstruction:
Setting: p = 6q+1 is prime. R is the set of cubic residues (nonzero cubes mod p). In the preceding sections Euler takes |R| = 2q, conditionally, because 1 has three cube roots mod p; he admits on p.48 that the full proof is still missing. N is the set of non-residues. From §388–389: R is closed under products and quotients (if mn and m lie in R, so does n). From §390: if a ∈ R then a^{2q} ≡ 1, since a = b^3 gives a^{2q} = b^{6q} ≡ 1 by Fermat. The problem served by this page is the converse of §390 (the cubic analogue of Euler's criterion), followed by the coset structure of the non-residues.

§391 (end), case 3 ∤ 2q. Write 2q = 3k ± 1 and suppose a^{2q} ≡ 1.
- If 2q = 3k+1: a^{3k+1} ≡ 1 = 1^3 is in R, and a^{3k} = (a^k)^3 is in R. By the quotient property, a ∈ R.
- If 2q = 3k−1: a^{3k} = a·a^{3k−1} ≡ a, so a is the cube (a^k)^3.
- Modern form (mine): gcd(3,2q) = 1, so 3u + 2qv = 1 for some u, v, and a = a^{3u}·a^{2qv} ≡ (a^u)^3.

§392, the remaining case 2q = 3k, i.e. p = 9k+1 (p ≡ 1 mod 9). One must show a^{3k} ≡ 1 implies a ∈ R. Euler notes that a^{3k} is trivially a cube, but this is not the point; the issue is that its residue equals 1.

Marginal note (*). Suppose a were a non-residue with a^{2q} ≡ 1. Then every non-residue (all have the form aα or a²α, α ∈ R) satisfies x^{2q} ≡ 1, since (aα)^{2q} = a^{2q}α^{2q} ≡ 1. All residues satisfy it too, so every number 1..p−1 would satisfy x^{2q} ≡ 1, which is absurd. The absurdity holds because a congruence of degree 2q < 6q cannot have 6q roots; Euler elsewhere proves this with finite differences. This argument presupposes the coset description proved only in §397–401.

§393. Euler offers a heuristic instead. The residues of 1, a, a², ... are '2q in number' like the cubic residues, both lists start with 1, and they share a³, a⁶, a⁹, .... Hence the list of powers 'can contain no term different from' R.

§394. Facts about non-residues:
- If mn ∈ R and m ∈ N, then n ∈ N (contrapositive of §389).
- A product of two non-residues need not be a residue.
- Residue × non-residue is always a non-residue.

§395. If A ∈ N then A² ∈ N, while A²·A = A³ ∈ R.

§396, proof of §395. If A² ∈ R then A^{4q} ≡ 1. Also A^{6q} ≡ 1, so A^{6q} − A^{4q} = A^{4q}(A^{2q} − 1) ≡ 0, giving A^{2q} ≡ 1. By the converse (§391–393), A ∈ R, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence A ∈ N implies A² ∈ N.

§397. Let R = {1, α, β, γ, ...} and A ∈ N. Then the lists A·R = {A, Aα, Aβ, ...} and A²·R = {A², A²α, ...} consist of non-residues. They are mutually distinct: Aα ≡ A²β would give A ≡ α/β ∈ R. Hence |N| ≥ 2|R|, matching the earlier claim |N| = 2|R|.

§398. If every number were a residue, then a^{2q} ≡ 1 for all a < p, which is absurd. So at least one non-residue exists, and with it 4q non-residues follow; only 2q distinct residues are possible.

§399. From one non-residue A come two classes, I = A·R and II = A²·R, each of size |R|.
- A product of two elements of the same class lies in the other class: Aα·Aβ = A²αβ, and A²α·A²β = A·(A³αβ).
- A product of one element from each class is a residue: Aα·A²β = A³αβ.

§400 (continued next page). Suppose some B ∈ N lies in neither class. Then B·R and B²·R are also non-residues; the contradiction is derived on p.50. In modern terms, R is the index-3 subgroup of (Z/p)^*, and I and II are its two non-trivial cosets.
errors: §393 is not a proof. The powers of a give ord(a) distinct residues, and ord(a) is only a divisor of 2q, not necessarily 2q. 'Sharing a³, a⁶, ... and other common properties' does not imply the powers of a lie in R; the real argument (subgroup of the cyclic group, or root counting) is missing. Euler evidently sensed this, hence the marginal note.

The marginal proof for §392 relies on §397–401: that every non-residue lies in a·R ∪ a²·R. In turn, §396 uses the converse criterion from §391–393 to conclude A ∈ R from A^{2q} ≡ 1. In the case 3 | q this is circular as written. A direct non-circular route exists: if A² ∈ R then A = A⁴/A³ ∈ R, using only §389.

§398 tacitly assumes |R| = 2q when it says 'eo ipso 4q non-residua sequuntur'. What follows from one non-residue alone is |N| ≥ 2|R|, hence |R| ≤ 2q. Equality needs the bound that x³ ≡ 1 has at most 3 roots, giving |R| ≥ 2q, or the coset exhaustion of §400–401.

The 'absurdum' in §398 and in the note (x^{2q} ≡ 1 for all x) is asserted without proof here. It is true, since a nonzero polynomial of degree 2q < p−1 has at most 2q roots mod p, but not justified on this page.

results.what: If p = 6q+1 is prime, 3 ∤ 2q and a^{2q} ≡ 1 (mod p), then a is a cubic residue.
results.modern_name: Euler's criterion for cubic residues (easy case gcd(3,(p−1)/3) = 1)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (Tractatus, c.1750, publ. 1849); general n-th power criterion via primitive roots, Gauss 1801

results.what: Attempted proof of the cubic criterion when 9 | p−1: a non-residue a with a^{2q} ≡ 1 would force x^{2q} ≡ 1 for all x.
results.modern_name: Euler's criterion for cubic residues via root counting / coset decomposition
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (stated); rigorous general proof Gauss, Disquisitiones 1801

results.what: Residue × non-residue is a non-residue; A ∈ N implies A² ∈ N; the non-residues split into the classes A·R and A²·R with the stated multiplication rules.
results.modern_name: Cosets of the index-3 subgroup of cubes in (Z/p)^*; (Z/p)^*/(cubes) ≅ Z/3

results.what: Exactly 2q cubic residues and 4q non-residues mod p = 6q+1.
results.modern_name: Index of the cubic-residue subgroup is 3

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known Euler Tractatus material on cubic residues, which historians (e.g. Lemmermeyer, Reciprocity Laws) already discuss. The arguments are standard, and the hard case is handled only heuristically.

checkable.sympy: set(pow(x,3,19) for x in range(1,19)) == set(a for a in range(1,19) if pow(a,6,19)==1)
checkable.asserts: Cubic criterion for p = 19 (q = 3, 2q = 3k case): cubes = solutions of a^{2q} ≡ 1.

checkable.sympy: set(pow(x,3,37) for x in range(1,37)) == set(a for a in range(1,37) if pow(a,12,37)==1)
checkable.asserts: Cubic criterion for p = 37, a case with 9 | p−1 (§392).

checkable.sympy: set(pow(x,3,31) for x in range(1,31)) == set(a for a in range(1,31) if pow(a,10,31)==1)
checkable.asserts: Cubic criterion for p = 31 (2q = 10, 3 ∤ 2q case of §391).

checkable.sympy: (lambda p,A: (lambda R: set((A*r)%p for r in R)|set((A*A*r)%p for r in R)|R == set(range(1,p)) and len(set((A*r)%p for r in R)&set((A*A*r)%p for r in R))==0)(set(pow(x,3,p) for x in range(1,p))))(37,2)
checkable.asserts: For p = 37 and non-residue A = 2, R, A·R and A²·R partition 1..36 (§397–399).

checkable.sympy: all((pow(A,2,37) not in set(pow(x,3,37) for x in range(1,37))) for A in range(1,37) if A not in set(pow(x,3,37) for x in range(1,37)))
checkable.asserts: §395/396: the square of a cubic non-residue is a non-residue (p = 37).
